To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the reentrant line can be modeled by means of a generalized stochastic Petri Net (GSPN); (ii) the GSPN model allows the seamless integration, in one formalism, of the logical/ structural and the timed-based behavior of the system; and (iii) the GSPNs provide a formal framework for the analytical characterization of the optimal scheduling policies for the reentrant line in its contemporary, automated, and more complex operational context.

the generalized stochastic Petri Nets provide a very effective and flexible framework for modeling, analyzing, and controlling the behavior of reentrant production systems, that the optimal policy is characterized as a threshold-based policy, and that the optimal threshold values can be computed analytically, using the proposed framework, as functions of the system parameters.

the optimal control policies for the reentrant line problem, in its contemporary operational context, are characterized by a complex, multi-dimensional structure that depends on both the system structure and the operational policies adopted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical framework for modeling and analyzing the performance of capacitated, flexible automated reentrant lines.
the development of an analytical framework for modeling, analyzing, and controlling flexibly automated reenant lines, and the development of new operational policies for them.
the development of new analytical models and tools for the performance analysis and control, of the scheduling problem in its modern context of automated, flexible manufacturing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the work presented in this paper constitutes a significant step towards the development of an analytical framework for addressing the scheduling problem for the contemporary reentrant lines, as they are typically implemented in the semiconductor fabrication plants.
the work presented in this paper is an important step in the direction of developing new scheduling policies and tools for the reentrant lines of the semiconductor industry.

the proposed framework constitutes the basis for the formal analysis of the reentrant lines in their most generic form and, hence, it can provide a solid analytical basis for the development of more effective and efficient scheduling tools and policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a generalized stochastic Petri-net model of reentrant lines that allows us to study their performance and control.

we are able to model the behavior of a capacitated reentrant line in a stochastic Petri net framework, and to derive an analytical formulation for its optimal scheduling problem, that is based on the minimization of a weighted sum of mean flow times and work-in-process (WIP) levels, for a given set of processing and buffer capacities.
it provides a new, more general analytical framework for the performance analysis and control (scheduling) of capacitated re-entrant lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed analytical framework provides the basis for a systematic approach to the development of new, robust, and stable scheduling tools and policies, for the control of the complex, flexibly automated, reentrant line scheduling problems.

it provides the analytical framework for the seamless integration of logical, structural, and timed-based aspects of system behavior, and leads to interesting qualitative characterizations of the structure of optimal scheduling policies.

it is possible to develop analytical models and tools to address the reentrant line problem in its contemporary operational context, which is much more complex than that of the classical, single-resource reentrant line.
